title: index not working when combine multiply fields using and operator
body:
Neo4J:5.10.0

Index create sql:
CREATE INDEX composite_IdxCompanyFilter FOR (n:`企业`) ON(n.city, n.province, n.district);

Query Sql:
explain MATCH (n:`企业`) where n.city = '重庆市' and n.province = '重庆市' and n.district = '万州区' RETURN n LIMIT 25

Expect:
all index filed can hit, but only city field is hitted
![image](https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/assets/26137810/f672ae8e-c8e1-4b23-b236-395372f2266e)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hello @reporter, thank you for reporting.

This is a known issue with `TEXT` indexes using `text-2.0` index provider. They have difficulty with estimating the number of unique items in the index (`estimatedUniqueSize` field below):

```json
{
  "updatesSinceEstimation": 0,
  "indexType": "TEXT",
  "totalSize": 10317493,
  "estimatedUniqueSize": 10317493
  "indexProvider": "text-2.0",
  "properties": ["city"],
  "labels": ["企业"],
},
{
  "updatesSinceEstimation": 0,
  "indexType": "TEXT",
  "totalSize": 10317493,
  "estimatedUniqueSize": 10317493
  "indexProvider": "text-2.0",
  "properties": ["province"],
  "labels": ["企业"],
},
{
  "updatesSinceEstimation": 0,
  "indexType": "TEXT",
  "totalSize": 10317493,
  "estimatedUniqueSize": 10317493
  "indexProvider": "text-2.0",
  "properties": ["district"],
  "labels": ["企业"],
},
{
  "updatesSinceEstimation": 0,
  "indexType": "RANGE",
  "totalSize": 10317493,
  "estimatedUniqueSize": 756
  "indexProvider": "range-1.0",
  "properties": ["city", "province", "district"],
  "labels": ["企业"],
},
```

As you can see, both `totalSize` and `estimatedUniqueSize` for the three TEXT indexes are set to 10317493, which is probably incorrect for you data. This mis-estimation makes the planner avoid using the composite index.

There are a few workarounds you can try:

- Add an index hint to your query:

```cypher
explain
MATCH (n:企业)
USING INDEX n:企业(city, province, district)
where n.city = '重庆市' and n.province = '重庆市' and n.district = '万州区'
RETURN n
LIMIT 25
```

- For the `TEXT` indexes listed above, do you have queries with `CONTAINS` or `ENDS WITH` that use them? If not, consider using `RANGE` indexes for those properties instead.
- If you _do_ have such queries, you can also try using `text-1.0` index provider for them instead, e.g. `CREATE TEXT INDEX FOR (n:企业) ON (n.city) OPTIONS { indexProvider: 'text-1.0' }`.

Hope this helps.

comments.body: @reporter You can run the query with `PROFILE` prefix and then get the text output from the browser (see the attached screenshot). If there's a lot of misses in `Page Cache Hits/Misses` column, the query might be slow because it's the first run.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @reporter The composite index is not used because you don't have predicates on all three properties. Only non-null properties are indexed, so you need to add `AND n.district IS NOT NULL` to be able to use the composite index for this query.
